table_title: List the MOOC-provider platforms appearing in Wikipedia's 'List of MOOC providers' master article that have their own English Wikipedia article, were founded between 2000 and 2020 inclusive, were currently operating at the snapshot date, AND whose Wikipedia article supplies a source-grounded founder cell (an explicit Founders / Founder(s) / Created-by infobox field, OR a body-text 'founded by' / 'co-founded by' / 'created by' / 'initiated by' / 'launched by' / 'founding partners' verb-phrase) — with the founding year, founder(s), and country of origin.
db_analog: SELECT platform, founded, founders, country_of_origin FROM mooc_providers WHERE founded BETWEEN 2000 AND 2020 AND has_english_wikipedia_article = true AND currently_operating = true AND has_source_grounded_founders = true ORDER BY platform
temporal_note: Wikipedia 'List of MOOC providers' master article + 13 per-platform articles + Wikimedia Foundation supporting article (added in cycle 10 to source-ground Wikiversity's Country of Origin via the parent Foundation's San Francisco HQ), accessed 2026-05-01 (re-validated 2026-05-06 during cycle-9 repair and 2026-05-11 during cycle-10 repair). Universe is MOOC-provider platforms appearing in the 'List of MOOC providers' master wikitable that have their own dedicated English Wikipedia article, were founded between 2000 and 2020 inclusive (per the per-platform Wikipedia article, which is preferred over the master-list 'Founded' column when the two disagree), were currently operating at the snapshot date, AND have a Founders cell that can be source-grounded from the cited per-platform Wikipedia article (via either an explicit `Founders` / `Founder(s)` / `Created by` infobox field, OR a body-text 'founded by' / 'co-founded by' / 'created by' / 'initiated by' / 'launched by' / 'founding partners' verb-phrase clause). Master-list entries excluded by the strict 5-clause filter, grouped by failure class: (a) source-grounded-Founders failures — France Université Numérique (Owner-only, no founder verb-phrase), openHPI (Owner-only), OpenLearning (Key people only, outside strict-policy allowed source labels), MIT OpenCourseWare ('initiative of MIT' is institutional but not within strict-policy verb-phrase list and no `Founders`/`Founder(s)`/`Created by` infobox field), OpenSAP ('provided by SAP' is institutional but not within strict-policy verb-phrase list); (b) own-article failures — Canvas Network (no own English Wikipedia article; redirects to Instructure parent); (c) pre-2000 founding-year failures — The Great Courses (per-platform article: founded 1990; master list also records 1990), LinkedIn Learning (per-platform article: founded 1995 as Lynda.com; master list also records 1995), Stanford Online (per-platform article: 'Stanford Online was founded in 1995 through the Stanford Center for Professional Development'; the master-list 'Founded' column shows 2006 but the per-platform article is preferred under the normalization rule, so this row fails the 2000-2020 filter), Open Universities Australia (per-platform article infobox `Established`: 1993; master-list 'Founded' shows 2013 but per-platform is preferred), Saylor Academy (per-platform article: founded 1999). Founding years 2006-2017 across all 13 rows. Founder cells are taken verbatim from each platform's Wikipedia article lead paragraph (preferred) or infobox 'Founders/Founder(s)/Created by' field; semicolon-delimited and alphabetized within each cell when multiple founders are named. Country of Origin is the country of the platform's headquarters per the cited Wikipedia article. Underlying facts (founding year, founders, origin country) are stable on a multi-decade horizon; the 'currently operating' filter is the only cell that changes over time, and master-list providers that shut down would be dropped on a future refresh.
_extraction_notes: Original instance filling the Education family-level gap. Source plan: Tier B Wikipedia, source_count = 15 (1 master 'List of MOOC providers' article anchoring the canonical universe + 13 per-platform Wikipedia articles supplying per-row attribute cells + 1 Wikimedia Foundation supporting article added in cycle 10 to source-ground Wikiversity's Country of Origin via the parent Foundation's San Francisco HQ). Per-platform infobox parsing across the master list was attempted programmatically with rowspan-aware HTML extraction; the heterogeneity of label conventions across platform articles (some use 'Founded', others 'Launched' or 'Formation'; some use 'Founder', others 'Founders' or 'Created by' or 'Owner'; some lack an explicit 'Headquarters' field) made fully-automated extraction unreliable, so per-platform cells were hand-curated from each article's lead paragraph + infobox cross-reference. Each cell traces to a specific platform's Wikipedia article by URL: Founded year matches the lead paragraph's stated founding year (e.g., Coursera's lead 'founded in 2012 by computer science professors Andrew Ng and Daphne Koller from Stanford University'); Founders match the lead's named-founders list; Country of Origin is the platform's headquarters country per the lead/infobox (7 United States, 2 Ireland, and 1 each of United Kingdom, Germany, France, India). Result: 13 rows x 4 columns, PK on Platform, 0 duplicates. Cycle-8 re-scope (Path B): the prior universe (cycles 1-7) was a multi-source-pattern '5-clause filter on MOOC-providers list OR cross-referenced edtech subcategories' set whose universe rule the cycle-7 audit ruled was not source-defined — the 'cross-referenced language-learning / coding / skills / K-12 / test-prep / tech-skills' clause had no canonical Wikipedia source-list anchor and was effectively curator-defined. Resolved by re-scoping to MOOC-providers-only: the universe is now exactly the entries on the 'List of MOOC providers' master wikitable that pass the 5-clause filter. Eighteen platforms from the cycle-7 universe were dropped: 17 non-MOOC platforms (Babbel, Brilliant, Busuu, Codecademy, CreativeLive, Duolingo, freeCodeCamp, Lingoda, Magoosh, MasterClass, Memrise, Outschool, Pluralsight, Quizlet, Skillshare, Treehouse, Unacademy) — none appear on the master list — and one non-master-list MOOC (XuetangX). Three master-list entries that pass the strict 5-clause filter were added in cycle 8: Shaw Academy (2013, James Egan; Adrian Murphy, Ireland — per article infobox `Founders` field), Stanford Online (cycle-8-staged at 2006, Stanford University, United States — but dropped in cycle 9 — see below), and Wikiversity (2006, Wikimedia community, United States — per article infobox `Created by` field). Cycle-9 repair (2026-05-06): cycle-8 audit raised one BLOCKING and one HYGIENE. (a) BLOCKING — Stanford Online founded-year discrepancy: the staged value 2006 was taken from the master 'List of MOOC providers' table, but the per-platform Stanford Online Wikipedia article body says 'Stanford Online was founded in 1995 through the Stanford Center for Professional Development'. Under the per-platform-article-preferred normalization rule, the per-platform article wins and Stanford Online's true founding year is 1995, which fails the 2000-2020 filter. Stanford Online dropped from the staged set; net universe 14 → 13. (b) HYGIENE — exclusion documentation drift: The Great Courses (1990) and LinkedIn Learning (1995) are master-list entries that fail the pre-2000 founding-year filter but were not enumerated in the prior exclusion documentation. Both added to the documented pre-2000 exclusion list, alongside Stanford Online (1995 per per-platform article), Open Universities Australia (1993 per infobox), and Saylor Academy (1999) — the pre-2000 exclusion class is now fully enumerated. The cycle-9 master-list completeness state: 24 master-list entries total = 13 staged + 11 documented exclusions split across 3 failure classes (5 source-grounded-Founders failures: FUN, openHPI, OpenLearning, MIT OCW, OpenSAP; 1 own-article failure: Canvas Network; 5 pre-2000 founding-year failures: Stanford Online (newly added in cycle 9 — master 2006 vs per-platform 1995), Open Universities Australia (master 2013 vs per-platform 1993, also a master-vs-per-platform discrepancy), Saylor Academy 1999, The Great Courses 1990, LinkedIn Learning 1995). The 'Primary Content Domain' column was dropped in cycle 8 because under MOOC-only scope every row would have Domain = 'MOOC' (zero calibration capacity); the schema is 4 columns, which still meets the multi_attribute_projection 1-key + ≥3-non-key minimum. Cycle-10 repair (2026-05-11): cycle-9 audit raised one BLOCKING and one NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE. (a) BLOCKING — Wikiversity Country of Origin not source-grounded: the cycle-8/9 staging assigned Wikiversity Country = United States, but the Wikiversity Wikipedia article does not directly state a country/HQ; its infobox supplies only `Owner: Wikimedia Foundation` and `Created by: Wikimedia community`. The US derivation comes from the Wikimedia Foundation's San Francisco HQ, which is sourced from the Wikimedia Foundation Wikipedia article — not from any URL currently in source_urls. Resolved by adding `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikimedia_Foundation` to source_urls (source_count 14 → 15), with the explicit derivation chain documented: Wikiversity infobox `Owner: Wikimedia Foundation` → Wikimedia Foundation article → 'Headquartered in San Francisco, California, United States'. (b) NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE — under-documented retained master-vs-per-platform discrepancies: in addition to the two pre-2000-filter discrepancies that pulled rows out (Stanford Online, Open Universities Australia), three retained rows have master-vs-per-platform 'Founded' value disagreements that the per-platform-preferred rule resolves silently. Documented in cycle 10: (i) Khan Academy — master list 2006 vs per-platform infobox `Launched: 2008`; staged 2008 (per-platform preferred). (ii) OpenClassrooms — master list 2007 vs per-platform article internal split (infobox `Launched: 10 November 1999` records the original Site du Zéro entity year; article lead 'Founded in 2013 by Pierre Dubuc and Mathieu Nebra, OpenClassrooms…' records the rebrand year of the OpenClassrooms brand); staged 2013 follows the article lead's brand-founding framing, treating 'OpenClassrooms' as the platform rather than the corporate entity. The Stanford-Online-vs-OpenClassrooms analogy is genuine but the two articles frame their founding-year statements differently: Stanford Online's article body says 'Stanford Online was founded in 1995' (single statement, no competing rebrand-year framing in the lead) so 1995 wins and the row is excluded; OpenClassrooms's article lead says 'Founded in 2013… OpenClassrooms' (brand-founding-year statement) and the 1999 infobox value refers to the pre-rebrand entity Site du Zéro, so 2013 wins and the row is retained. (iii) Udacity — master list 2012 vs per-platform infobox internal split (`Founded: June 2011` corporate founding vs `Launched: February 2012` product launch); staged 2011 prefers the `Founded` field, the more conventional sense of 'founding year'. Net cycle-10 universe: 13 → 13 (no row changes; only source_count +1 and narrative-completeness corrections).
